provider.notes: The vendor id for speech-to-text models deployed in Azure OpenAI. It is not Azure AI Speech, which is the separate provider id azure (microsoft-azure). The two spellings are AZURE_OPENAI_NAMES in gateway/src/core/tts/self_hosted.rs:112, matched by is_azure_openai (:131-134). The id is recognised but has no speech-to-text plugin (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs registers it for text-to-speech at :1826 and as a realtime alias at :2007-2008 only); a live call that names such a deployment is refused today with the codes unsupported_deployment and stt_not_streaming (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 and :815-826), which integration decisions addendum A1 keeps for an Azure OpenAI deployment the segmented engine does not cover, until the Bud-side check on them is answered. The upload route forwards the file whole (gateway/src/handlers/transcribe.rs:839-913). On Azure the model string on the wire is the name the customer gave the deployment, and it goes into the URL path (self_hosted.rs:171-200). budapp publishes the credential's deployment id in voice_table.model when there is one and the model name otherwise (transcribe.rs:827-829). Today's leg code sends config.stt.model when set, otherwise voice_table.model (bud_legs.rs:216-226). Because a deployment name says nothing about the base model, a row is found from the base model the deployment override declares (underlying_model), else from the name itself, which matches an exact or pattern row only when the customer named the deployment after the base model, else the provider default row, which is file upload. The name sent to Azure is always the deployment name. default_model is null because there is no deployment to fall back to; an empty model is a configuration error (self_hosted.rs:177-183).

provenance.notes: Provider default: what a deployment name resolves to when nothing declares its base model. It fails slow. Every Azure OpenAI model served by the /audio interface is file-only, so file upload is right for all of them. It is wrong only for a deployment of a realtime-only base model (gpt-live-transcribe, gpt-realtime-whisper), where each upload would be rejected by Azure; such a deployment must declare its base model. In Bud a realtime transcription deployment is published with the capability realtime_session, and the gateway's leg resolver accepts only deployments with the capability audio_transcription as a speech-to-text leg (bud_legs.rs:31, :812), so the wrong case is not expected to be reachable through Bud today.

transports.disabled_reason: Not implemented. The gateway has no per-utterance upload adapter; its only Azure OpenAI transcription code is a whole-file passthrough on the upload route, and a live call that names such a deployment is refused before any client is built (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 and :815-826). Even once the adapter exists, Azure's default quota of 3 audio requests per minute cannot carry a conversation, so a quota increase is a precondition and its absence must be reported as a configuration warning at session start.

latency.notes: Microsoft publishes no latency for the audio API on short clips.

gateway_client.notes: The multipart body is OpenAI's, but the address is {api_base}/openai/deployments/{deployment}/audio/transcriptions?api-version=... and the key travels in an api-key header, never in Authorization (self_hosted.rs:125; transcribe.rs:1023-1025). The address must be https and must pass the private-address filter, so an Azure Private Link endpoint is refused today (self_hosted.rs:215-228). The gateway sends api-version 2025-04-01-preview unless the deployment sets provider_params.api_version (self_hosted.rs:115; gateway/src/handlers/openai_audio.rs:1557-1561). The existing code has a 300 second deadline, returns the body unparsed and has no circuit breaker, so only its request half can be reused. Azure ignores stream=true for this model, so text never arrives in pieces. verbose_json is accepted and Microsoft says it returns per-segment probabilities, but the field names are not spelled out on the Azure pages, so no quality signal is claimed until a live response has been read.

segment_profile.rationale: Azure's default quota for the speech-to-text audio API is 3 requests per minute. One upload per caller turn is the most that quota can carry, so segments are held and uploaded once per turn, one at a time. Restore the gateway defaults (upload at each pause, two in flight) only for a deployment whose quota increase is confirmed.

Restore the gateway defaults (upload at each pause, two in flight) only for a deployment whose quota increase is confirmed.

refusal.text: Azure OpenAI serves this model by transcribing one uploaded audio file per request; it has no live streaming interface. This gateway does not yet serve it on a live call for this deployment. Use the deployment for file transcription, choose a streaming transcription deployment for the call, or ask the operator to enable segmented speech-to-text for this deployment.

transports.disabled_reason: Before Release 4 the gateway has no speech-to-text client for the OpenAI Realtime transcription session; its only code for that socket is a pass-through relay. Release 4 adds the gateway-driven commit client for OpenAI and Azure OpenAI (addendum B11), enabled for Azure only after a live probe with a real deployment.

gateway_client.code_ref: relay only: gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/upstream.rs:113-191 (builds {base}/realtime?intent=transcription for openai and /openai/v1/realtime?intent=transcription with an api-key header for azure_openai); session and event types to reuse: gateway/src/core/realtime/openai/protocol.rs
gateway_client.notes: How the session must work: open the socket with intent=transcription; send session.update with session.type set to transcription, input format audio/pcm at 24 kHz (the gateway must resample from the caller's rate), the transcription model, and turn_detection null; append base64 audio continuously; when the gateway's own voice detector decides the utterance has ended, send input_audio_buffer.commit. Text arrives as conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta while the caller speaks and as ...completed after the commit. Completions for different turns may arrive out of order and must be matched by item_id. A commit on an empty buffer is an error. The live models reject the vendor's own voice detection, which is why the gateway owns endpointing here. The intent=transcription query is what the gateway relay, Pipecat and LiveKit dial and what Microsoft's sample uses; it is absent from OpenAI's own pages. The language and context fields are left out of this profile because they differ by model (languages and keywords on gpt-live-transcribe, language and no prompt on gpt-realtime-whisper) and a profile cannot see the model. On Azure the socket is wss://{resource}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/realtime?intent=transcription with an api-key header and no api-version; the deployment name goes in session.audio.input.transcription.model. Microsoft's sample sets turn_detection to none and sends the commit itself at 24 kHz. A session lasts at most 60 minutes, so a longer call needs a reconnect.

provenance.notes: On Azure the id sent on the wire is the customer's deployment name, so this row matches only when the deployment override declares this base model or when the deployment happens to be named after it; see the provider notes. No file interface exists for this model, so the only way to reach it on a live call is a socket on which the gateway's own voice detector sends the commit, and that client does not exist yet. In Bud a realtime transcription deployment is published with the capability realtime_session, which the gateway's leg resolver does not accept as a speech-to-text leg (it requires audio_transcription; bud_legs.rs:31, :812), so wiring it also needs a change there. Version 2026-07-29; Microsoft calls it the 'current recommended model for realtime transcription scenarios'. On OpenAI's service the model takes languages (plural), keywords and a prompt, and returns no word timestamps, speaker labels or confidence. Enabled from Release 4 on 2026-10-04 (addendum B11), gated on a live probe.

provenance.notes: On Azure the id sent on the wire is the customer's deployment name, so this row matches only when the deployment override declares this base model or when the deployment happens to be named after it; see the provider notes. No file interface exists for this model, so the only way to reach it on a live call is a socket on which the gateway's own voice detector sends the commit, and that client does not exist yet. In Bud a realtime transcription deployment is published with the capability realtime_session, which the gateway's leg resolver does not accept as a speech-to-text leg (it requires audio_transcription; bud_legs.rs:31, :812), so wiring it also needs a change there. Version 2026-05-06, described as an 'audio model for real-time low-latency transcription'. On OpenAI's service the model rejects a prompt and takes a singular language; OpenAI's pages disagree on whether the delay setting applies only to it. A third-party benchmark of OpenAI's own endpoint measured a median of 740 ms and a 99th percentile of 1080 ms from end of speech to final text; that figure is not recorded as this row's latency because it was not measured on Azure. Enabled from Release 4 on 2026-10-04 (addendum B11), gated on a live probe.
